title: AdaptHealth / Ahern Rentals / Alliance Holdings GP / Armada Hoffler / Accredited Mortgage REIT Preferred / Aspen Insurance / American Home Mortgage — Security Path, Recovery and Funding V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: Ahern Rentals 2012; Alliance Holdings GP 2009, 2012 and 2016; AHHAP 2012; Aspen Insurance 2011; American Home Mortgage 2007.
AHM 2005 is a genuine Short even though many neighboring raw is_short=true records are actually Longs; direction was determined from explicit action language in each source description.
Only Armada Hoffler 2015 has a source performance row. Its price factors imply approximately +14.75% at 1Y, +71.63% at 2Y, +91.45% at 3Y and +146.04% at 5Y.
Ahern Rentals second-lien notes were bought at 65; the confirmed plan paid par plus pre-petition interest, making the credit successful even though holders did not receive reorganized equity.
AHGP 2012 outcome is supported by the same author's 2016 follow-up saying the Alliance position was sold in late 2013 in the $60s.
AHGP 2016 explicitly underwrote distribution-cut risk; the cut happened, then units recovered to roughly $28 by the 2018 ARLP simplification.

AHHAP original remaining liquidation estimate was $6.64-$8.37 at a $6 price; final aggregate distributions were $19.27/share, implying roughly $9.77/share of distributions after subtracting the ~$9.50/share already paid before the VIC date.
Aspen Insurance rerated toward book by 2013-14 and was later acquired by Apollo for $42.75/share cash in 2019.

American Home Mortgage provides a paired falsification case: the 2005 Short focused on cash/funding structure and succeeded, while the 2007 Long focused on borrower credit quality/book value and failed catastrophically within five months.

AdaptHealth 2022 correctly diagnosed a 2020 integration problem but overestimated the durability of M&A economics; large goodwill impairments and weak 2026 equity value invalidate the per-share compounding case.

batch_lessons: Direction metadata must be validated against explicit buy/short language in the thesis, especially when one raw flag maps to both longs and shorts.
An operating turnaround does not automatically validate acquisition ROIC or per-share compounding.
In distressed credit, recovery coverage is more robust than predicting exactly which reorganization plan will win.
Low-cost commodity producers have survival and share-gain advantages but remain highly cyclical securities.
Headline distribution yield should be stress-tested against cycle-low free cash flow and debt service.
An internal REIT development platform can create value above static NAV through development-to-stabilized-value spreads.
Liquidation analysis must subtract distributions already received before the investor purchase date.
Insurance P/B works best when book value itself compounds; cheap book without book growth is not enough.
For leveraged financial companies, liability funding and collateral liquidity can dominate borrower credit quality.
Multiple funding facilities are not true diversification if they depend on the same collateral market and confidence regime.
The same company can support entirely different valid thesis types at different prices and cycle states.
Paired long/short write-ups on the same company are especially valuable for identifying which evidence was genuinely causal.
